articles.title: Martin Luther King Jr was born in this two-storey Atlanta house in 1929 and spent his first 12 years there; visitors can now explore the family home on free ranger-led tours
articles.summary: Martin Luther King Jr birth home, Atlanta, the two-storey house at 501 Auburn Avenue is where the civil rights leader was born on 15 January 1929 and
articles.body: Martin Luther King Jr birth home, Atlanta, the two-storey house at 501 Auburn Avenue is where the civil rights leader was born on 15 January 1929 and lived for the first twelve years of his life. It stands in the residential section of Sweet Auburn, the centre of Black Atlanta. Today the property operates as a historic site, and visitors can enter the home only on a guided tour led by a park ranger. Its frame construction, Queen Anne style and its place on Auburn Avenue, the street of his family’s church and the King Centre, shape the entire visit.A 1926 marriage brought Michael Luther King into the household, and three children were born thereAccording to the National Park Service, the house was built in 1895 for a white family. Reverend Adam Daniel Williams, pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church, bought it in 1909 for $3,500. He moved in with his wife, Jennie Celeste, and their six-year-old daughter, Alberta Christine, the only one of their three children to survive infancy.On 25 November 1926, Christine married a minister named Michael Luther King at her father’s church. Instead of Christine leaving, her new husband moved into the family home with her parents. Three children were born there: Willie Christine, Michael Jr, who later became known as Martin Luther King Jr, and Alfred Daniel.The King Centre said the household was larger than one family. Martin Luther King Jr lived there with his grandparents, parents and siblings, as well as other relatives and boarders.From a rental property to a museum; how the home was kept after the family moved to BoulevardReverend Williams died of a heart attack in the house on 21 March 1931. His wife later died of a heart attack too, and the King family then moved to a new home at 193 Boulevard. The old house stayed in the family and became a rental property.National Park Service said plans to restore it as a historic museum began after the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr on 4 April 1968.How Ebenezer Baptist Church on Auburn Avenue tied three generations of the family to one pulpitHis maternal grandfather, Reverend Williams, became the second pastor of Ebenezer Baptist Church in 1893. Martin Luther King Sr. served as the third pastor from 1933 until he retired in 1975.Martin Luther King Jr served as co-pastor from 1947 until he left for Crozer Theological Seminary in September 1948. He returned as co-pastor from 1960 until his assassination in 1968. The church, at 407 Auburn Avenue, was restored in 2011 to its appearance during those final years.How to tour the birth home, free ranger-led visits, same-day registration and limited group sizesVisitors register in person on the day of the tour at the information desk of the visitor centre, as The King Centre explained, and no reservations are possible. Tours fill first come, first served, and they go quickly at weekends and on holidays. Groups can reserve up to three spaces on the day.The King Centre’s visitor guide lists tours every day, starting at 10 in the morning with the last at 5 in the afternoon. articles.title: Guns, money and neutrality collide as Switzerland prepares for crucial vote
articles.summary: Switzerland's century-old policy of neutrality is heading for a crucial test as the country prepares to vote on whether its weapons should be allowed to
articles.body: Switzerland's century-old policy of neutrality is heading for a crucial test as the country prepares to vote on whether its weapons should be allowed to reach a wider group of western nations, even those involved in armed conflicts.The November 29 referendum has opened a battle between Switzerland's defence industry, which wants greater access to international markets, and neutrality advocates who fear that easing export restrictions could compromise the country's long-standing position as a neutral state.According to Reuters, the proposed amendments to Switzerland's War Materiel Act would allow arms exports to 36 western countries, including the United States, European Union members and Japan, even when they are involved in armed conflicts, provided the weapons are not intended for use in those conflicts. Ukraine, however, would remain excluded from the arrangement.The proposed changes would also scrap the general requirement for countries purchasing Swiss weapons to sign declarations prohibiting their re-export to third countries without prior approval from Bern. The government could still demand such assurances on a case-by-case basis.Supporters of the amendment argue that these restrictions are hurting domestic manufacturers and weakening Switzerland's position in Europe's defence supply chains.Centre Party lawmaker Reto Nause said the legislation needed to reflect the deteriorating international security environment."We're facing a level of threat we haven't seen since the Second World War," Nause said, arguing that Switzerland needed to preserve its domestic arms production capacity and expertise in critical military technologies.The referendum has significant implications for Switzerland's defence manufacturing sector, which employs around 14,000 people and exported military equipment worth approximately $1.15 billion in 2025, according to Reuters.Switzerland was the world's 17th-largest arms exporter over the past decade, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.Matthias Zoller, general secretary of the Swiss Aeronautics, Security and Defence Association, described the referendum as decisive for the sector's future."This is decisive, it's really 'go' or 'no go' for the future of the Swiss arms industry," Zoller said.Why Swiss neutrality is at the centre of the debateOpponents of the proposed changes argue that easing export restrictions could undermine Switzerland's traditional neutrality by allowing its weapons to reach countries involved in armed conflicts.Switzerland's neutrality is rooted in the 1907 Hague Conventions, which prohibit neutral states from participating in armed conflicts and providing military support to belligerents. However, international neutrality law does not impose a blanket ban on arms exports. Switzerland's existing restrictions are also based on domestic legislation that goes beyond the minimum requirements of international neutrality law.Mirjam Hostetmann, leader of the youth wing of the Social Democratic Party, which opposes the proposed changes, warned that relaxing export restrictions could increase the risk of Swiss weapons reaching civil wars and governments accused of violating international norms."It's an illusion to believe that more weapons will guarantee more peace," she said, adding that the proposed changes would benefit the arms industry rather than the wider public.The referendum has exposed divisions across Switzerland's political landscape. While the Social Democrats and Greens are leading opposition to the changes, the Swiss People's Party, along with other centre-right parties, supports easing export restrictions. However, some SVP members have broken ranks to oppose the amendment, highlighting divisions within the right-wing camp.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Odyssey cruise ship that left 200 passengers stranded, impounded in Singapore
articles.summary: A cruise ship whose passengers were left stranded in Cambodia after its operator ran out of money has been seized by authorities in Singapore, where it
articles.body: A cruise ship whose passengers were left stranded in Cambodia after its operator ran out of money has been seized by authorities in Singapore, where it arrived on Sunday.The Odyssey, which was supposed to take passengers on a continuous journey around the world, was impounded following its arrival from Cambodia. Around 200 guests had been forced to leave the vessel at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville after its US-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, suspended operations.Singapore's Maritime and Port Authority confirmed that the ship had been seized following a court order."The vessel has been placed under arrest pursuant to a court order," the authority said in a statement, without providing further details.It added that the crew were safe and that arrangements for their welfare were being handled by the ship's creditors. "There are no passengers on board," the statement said.The authority also confirmed that the vessel "is currently anchored in Singapore port waters".The ship had reached Sihanoukville last month as part of its scheduled itinerary. However, passengers were caught off guard when Villa Vie Residences announced that it was suspending the cruise's operations, bringing the planned round-the-world voyage to an abrupt halt nearly two years after it began.The company blamed "extraordinary increases" in fuel costs linked to the US-Israel war with Iran for its decision.The Odyssey had been marketed as an affordable way to travel around the world, with customers given the option of buying or renting cabins either for a holiday or as a permanent residence.Some passengers reportedly sold all their possessions to afford the journey. They were given just seven hours to pack their belongings and leave the 200-metre-long vessel, which had been carrying 203 guests and 156 crew members.Villa Vie said the monthly fuel cost for each cabin had risen from an average of $1,800 to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000 in parts of Asia, making it increasingly difficult to keep the voyage running.You use AI every day. articles.title: In his memoir, Biden says Jan 6 Capitol attack will follow Trump to his grave
articles.summary: Former US President Joe Biden has said that the January 6, attack on the US Capitol will follow Donald Trump to his grave, accusing his successor of
articles.body: Former US President Joe Biden has said that the January 6, attack on the US Capitol will follow Donald Trump to his grave, accusing his successor of undermining American democracy and damaging democratic institutions.The first excerpt of the memoir was published by The Atlantic on Monday. The book is scheduled for release on November 17."Donald Trump led an insurrection," Biden wrote, referring to the attack by Trump's supporters as Congress met to certify Biden's 2020 election victory.Rejecting the description of the rioters as peaceful protesters, Biden said they had come armed to stop the certification of a legitimate election."What Trump did on January 6, 2021, should never be forgotten. It should follow him to his grave," he wrote.Biden also accused Trump of undermining his administration's achievements, particularly policies aimed at tackling climate change, and criticised his Department of Government Efficiency."In my case, that feeling was magnified by the dismissive and destructive nature of Donald Trump, who seemed unable to tolerate the idea that someone else's accomplishments might be worth building on rather than tearing down," Biden wrote.Biden reflects on presidency and healthBiden also defended his four-year presidency, which was marked by the Covid-19 pandemic, economic concerns and questions about his age and fitness for office.He abandoned his re-election bid after a poor debate performance against Trump in June 2024. His vice-president, Kamala Harris, subsequently lost the November election to Trump.In a social media post on Sunday, Biden said the book would explain the challenges he faced and the decisions he made as president.Biden, who announced his prostate cancer diagnosis months after leaving office, said his health would limit his promotional activities.His doctors remain encouraged by his response to treatment, he said, adding: "Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down."Biden recalls cordial meeting with TrumpBiden also recounted an Oval Office meeting with Trump days after the 2020 election, when the latter reportedly told him: "You know, Joe, if it weren't for politics, I believe we'd be good friends."Biden said he briefed Trump on the Russia-Ukraine war, Nato, Israel and Gaza, and US-China relations. However, he felt Trump was more interested in the personalities of world leaders than international affairs.The meeting left Biden worried that Trump would dismantle his administration's achievements. He said Trump's early executive orders after returning to office confirmed those concerns.The memoir's title echoes Biden's earlier book, Promise Me, Dad, which chronicled his son Beau's battle with cancer and death in 2015.In Sunday's post, Biden reiterated his belief that America was "built on an idea" that "all of us are created equal"."Promise me, America," he concluded, "that we'll never forget it."You use AI every day. articles.title: After Karnataka's E20 shocker, Keralam collects petrol samples to check ethanol content
articles.summary: KOCHI: After Karnataka raised concerns over excess ethanol blending in petrol, Food and Civil Supplies minister Anoop Jacob on Monday said Keralam had
articles.body: KOCHI: After Karnataka raised concerns over excess ethanol blending in petrol, Food and Civil Supplies minister Anoop Jacob on Monday said Keralam had begun collecting petrol samples from across the state to check whether the ethanol content was within the prescribed limits, according to news agency ANI.Jacob said the samples had been sent to laboratories for testing and the results were awaited. He described the issue raised by Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar as a "major concern" across the country.Speaking to the media, the minister said, "We are collecting random samples from across the state to see if ethanol is within the prescribed limits or not. The civil supplies commission has been authorised to do that. And now, from the northern districts and from the southern districts also, we are taking random samples."The samples are being collected in all the prescribed formats. We are following and complying with all the protocols. And we have also requested that oil company representatives be present where we are collecting the samples. After that, we will be sending the samples to the government-owned chemical labs, and after the results come, we will take further steps if it is necessary," the minister added.Jacob said consumers had the right to know how much ethanol was blended into petrol, as it could affect vehicles and reduce mileage. He also urged people to keep politics out of the issue, saying consumers should be informed about the quality of the fuel they use.He said, "It's a major concern what DK Shivakumar has expressed. It's a major concern not only in Kerala or Karnataka, but it's also across the country. The consumers have the right to know what they are using," minsiter said." Whether the ethanol is of a cheaper quality or whether the ethanol is above the prescribed limits, all this should be conveyed to the customers. They have the right to know... This is not a matter of politics or something. It's a concern that has arisen. Many vehicles are getting damaged. The mileage is coming down. Many such issues have arisen. I don't think politics should be mixed with this," minister added.Meanwhile, the Keralam Civil Supplies Department conducted an inspection at fuel stations in Kochi to check the ethanol content in E20 petrol. District Civil Supplies Officer Shaji PR said officials had collected six samples, each measuring one litre, and sent two of them to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada for testing. The results are awaited."We conducted an inspection... We have inspected the details of the quantity of ethanol in the motor spirit, ordinary petrol. There were six samples at the rate of one litre taken. We sent two samples to an analytical chemical laboratory in Kakinada. We are waiting for the result," Shaji PR told ANI.The inspections come amid concerns raised by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad over the impact of petrol containing more than 20% ethanol on vehicles. He warned that higher ethanol concentrations could damage components in vehicles not designed to handle such fuel.At a press conference on November 6, Arshad said the Karnataka government had collected 63 samples from different locations across the state and from all major oil companies.Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology had claimed that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contained between 26% and 31% ethanol.However, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said all 893 samples of E20 petrol collected from public sector oil marketing companies across 27 states and Union Territories had met the prescribed quality standards, countering claims of excessive ethanol blending.Three state-run oil marketing companies — Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited — also said ethanol blending was a controlled and automated process carried out under statutory guidelines rather than through manual intervention.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.title: As a boy, Richard Childress sold popcorn and peanuts at a North Carolina track; he later built a NASCAR team that won 14 national-series titles
articles.summary: As a boy, Richard Childress sold popcorn and peanuts at a North Carolina track; he later built a NASCAR team that won 14 national-series titles
articles.body: Richard childress’s journey into American motorsports began far from the victory celebrations and championship trophies associated with NASCAR. As a young boy growing up in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, he sold popcorn and peanuts at Bowman Gray Stadium, a local short-track racing venue, to help support his family. According to Richard Childress's official racing history, his boyhood interest in the sport led him to make racing his career in the 1970s with the formation of his Richard Childress Racing team Organisation, now one of the three-based teams at NASCAR. As a team owner, he has earned 14 NASCAR national series championships, including six with the racing legend Dale Earnhardt racing with him in the top division.From selling snacks at Bowman Gray Stadium to becoming a racerBorn on 21st September 1945 in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, Childress's first introduction to racing was when he was in the stands at Bowman Grey Stadium as a 13-year-old, selling popcorn and peanuts with his brother. Their earnings from the job helped support their family, and he enjoyed being close to the sport. While watching local drivers race, he took a liking to stock car racing and was a fan of drivers Cale Yarborough and David Pearson.His Focus then shifted from just attending the races to competing in them. As a 17-year-old, he bought a used 1947 Plymouth that had previously been a taxi cab for just $20 and, with a group of friends, turned it into a racecar. His first shot at competing in a NASCAR event was in September 1969 at SuperSpeedway, when all the drivers of the day decided to forfeit the race after a disagreement over the safety of the sport. Childress competed and was placed 23rd.But it wasn't easy to become a driver. Unlike factory-backed drivers, independent racers had to find their own sponsorship, keep their car in shape, and also cover the cost of travel. Childress held down other jobs to keep his desire, often putting in 18 to 20 hours a day between jobs and races.Building a racing organisation and partnering with Dale EarnhardtHe competed as a driver for more than 10 years while building his team. Richard Childress Racing was founded in 1969 as a small, almost one-man organisation. He did many different jobs, serving as both driver and mechanic, as well as preparing the cars' engines. He racked up 76 top-10 finishes out of 285 top-tier NASCAR starts from 1969 to 81 but realised that his best shot at lasting place was to be a team owner. Childress quit driving in 1981 and began to focus more heavily on his operation. In 1983, the team called its first big triumph with Ricky Rudd.Dale Earnhardt's advent in 1984 was another milestone. Their pairing became one of the most successful in the history of the sport. Earnhardt competed for RCR, winning 6 premier series titles in 1986, 1987, 1990, 1991, 1993 and 1994. The partnership delivered 67 race wins from 1984 to 2000. Earnhardths achievement helped to establish RCR as a leading organisation while continuing to invest in his facilities, personnel and competitive efforts. The tie-up was founded on a common desire to race at the highest level regularly. Earnhardt's career success contributed significantly to Childress's reputation as a team owner. Expanding RCR and establishing a championship legacyAs the organisation expanded, Childress grew beyond the top level of NASCAR to races and other national series. RCR earned its first NASCAR Truck Series championship in 1995 with driver Mick Skinner. Several years later, Kevin Harvick won the organisation's first Busch Series championship in 2001, making Childress the first team owner to win a championship in each of NASCAR's three major national series. Successes also came along with a variety of other drivers. Harvick again clinched the Busch Series crown in 2006, and so did Childress's grandson Austin Dillon in 2013. Furthermore, Tyler Reddick took the 2019 Xfinity Series title. These results showed how the organisation kept on promoting new drivers and racing in multiple divisions.The NASCAR Hall of Fame's Historical profile credited Childress with 14 owner Championships across the national series of the sport. According to its pre-existing stat sheet, he was enshrined in the Hall of Fame in 2017 for his involvement in the sport. Today, Richard Childress Racing is based on a new 600-acre campus in Welcome, North Carolina, and contains a team shop, manufacturing facility, an engineering centre, and a competition department. It started as a fascination with the sport as a young boy at Bowman Gray Stadium and has turned into a motorsport institution.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari on Monday defended herself after facing criticism for claiming that bursting firecrackers helps kill germs
articles.body: NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari on Monday defended herself after facing criticism for claiming that bursting firecrackers helps kill germs and viruses.The actor-turned-politician said her statements were being deliberately twisted to garner TRP."Whenever I say something, people who oppose me use it to increase their TRP and views. Even if I cough or sneeze, the 'seku-maku' (a Bengali slang meaning secular and Marxists) pick it up," Adhikari told a Bengali TV channel."What I meant was that bursting firecrackers during Diwali-Kali Puja night kills germs, as told by our grandmothers and elders for generations. Lighting lamps drives away evil forces," she added.Later in the day, the BJP MLA apologised for her remarks and said: "There is an old saying from our ancestors regarding these traditions. In essence, this is a festival of lights - a festival of lighting lamps - meant to eradicate social evils. In the past, through rituals, many such evils were addressed. Now, however, we live in the era of firecrackers, and given how much science has advanced, perhaps that perspective is no longer appropriate."If anyone has been hurt, I apologise. I am willing to retract my statement; consider it withdrawn. But the core idea remains: such social evils were - and still can be - eradicated."Adhikari was trolled for claiming at a Kali Puja pandal inauguration in her Tollygunge constituency on Saturday that bursting firecrackers could cure several diseases.While addressing a gathering, a firecracker exploded loudly in front of her.Continuing her speech, she said, "You will see that bursting firecrackers will cure several diseases. Our chief minister has said that we will burst firecrackers. How can Kali Puja be complete without green firecrackers? We will definitely burst green firecrackers.""However, we will follow the guidelines issued by the police," she added.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday said the administration had taken necessary measures to enforce the Supreme Court's guidelines on noise pollution, though he acknowledged that some firecrackers were burst beyond the permitted hours.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: An amateur prospector who had spent several days swinging a metal detector on an outback station near Tibooburra, New South Wales, dug up a 1.2-kg gold nugget worth about A$150,000 from a faint signal
articles.summary: An amateur prospector spent several days swinging a metal detector across the red dirt of Mount Stuart Station near Tibooburra, New South Wales, before a
articles.body: An amateur prospector spent several days swinging a metal detector across the red dirt of Mount Stuart Station near Tibooburra, New South Wales, before a faint signal stopped him in his tracks. What he uncovered was a quartz-flecked gold nugget weighing 1,218 grams, with testing showing about 940 grams of pure gold, worth roughly A$150,000 to A$160,000 at spot prices and potentially up to A$200,000 to a collector. The lucky finder, who wishes to remain anonymous, has nicknamed the discovery the Tibooburra Spud, as per reports by ABC News, 1 News, and Perth Now.The find is remarkable not just for its size, but for how close it came to being missed. The prospector told ABC News that the signal was not loud for the size of the piece, and that he had nearly walked past it before deciding to dig. Read more about this fascinating discovery here:A faint signal in the red dirtThe prospector had been fossicking for years and was used to coming up empty. He told ABC News that most of what he digs up is rubbish, including lead bullets, old-timer’s nails and horseshoes. In mid-October, while finishing up a day of searching, his Gold Monster 2000 detector picked up a signal. He said it was not loud for the size of the piece, but once he got down to about 100 millimetres, the machine began squealing. After a few scrapes of dirt, he spotted a bright yellow dot in the centre of the hole. Footage of the discovery shows the prospector laughing in disbelief as he brushes dirt away from the nugget, which he initially worried might be a painted rock.What the nugget is worthThe nugget weighs 1,218 grams, with testing showing about 940 grams is pure gold. At spot prices, ABC News estimates its value between A$150,000 and A$160,000.The prospector believes a collector could pay as much as A$200,000 for the specimen, given its size and character. PerthNow reported the same range, noting that the nugget’s rough, irregular shape and quartz flecks add to its appeal.The find is rare enough that Greg Spangler, who has sold prospecting supplies in Broken Hill for more than 20 years, said he has only seen one other person find a nugget heavier than a kilogram. Most finds are gold flakes or small nuggets weighing a few ounces.Why Tibooburra draws prospectorsGold prospecting around Tibooburra dates back to the late 1880s and remains a major drawcard for tourists. The remote town sits in far western New South Wales, close to the Queensland and South Australian borders.Fossicking on the Tibooburra Common, the land surrounding the township, is currently banned while Native Title permissions are being pursued. However, at least two stations in the region, Mount Stuart and Gumvale, allow fossicking for a fee.Spangler said the hobby could keep going forever, because every time it rains, people find gold where they did not before. He also noted that rising gold prices have drawn more people to prospecting, with prices peaking in January at almost A$8,000 per troy ounce before settling around A$5,700.A hobby with more than moneyBeyond the chance of an instant boost to a retirement fund, Spangler said prospecting offers other benefits. He described the experience of getting up in the morning, being the first to see the sunrise, and enjoying the peace and quiet of the outback.He also sees it as a pastime the whole family can be involved in. For the prospector who found the Tibooburra Spud, the reward was both financial and personal, a moment of pure excitement after years of digging through dirt and metal scraps.His advice to would-be fossickers is simple: keep walking, keep swinging and keep digging every target. For him, that persistence is what turned a faint signal in the red dirt into a discovery worth more than most people earn in a year.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1981, New Mexico moved bighorn sheep into the Peloncillo Mountains; after contact with Arizona sheep, every transplanted Red Rock animal died of pneumonia
articles.summary: Discover the unexpected outcomes of New Mexico's bighorn sheep transplant in the Peloncillo Mountains. Learn how a pneumonia outbreak influenced wildlife recovery efforts and the lasting impact of disease contact between sheep populations.
articles.body: Sometimes a wildlife project ends in a way nobody expected. In 1981 and 1982, New Mexico moved bighorn sheep into the Peloncillo Mountains. Amy S. Fisher, New Mexico Department of Game and Fish, reported in a 1991 report published in the Desert Bighorn Council Transactions that, after contact with Arizona sheep, every Red Rock sheep moved there died of bronchopneumonia. The report is short, but there is a clear lesson about how fragile wildlife recovery can be. It also shows how careful follow-up can answer difficult questions even years later.A move that ended in tragedy Fisher’s report lists 38 sheep transplanted into the Peloncillo Mountains in 1981 and 1982. Red Rock sheep were released there together with bighorns from Arizona. Red Rock is a captive herd which, by 1990, numbered 80 individuals. However, the Peloncillo story went very differently. According to Fisher, all the Red Rock sheep released to the range died from bronchopneumonia, an infectious lung disease, after coming into contact with the Arizona sheep. There is no information provided as to how the disease spread. The remaining herd never grew. Between 1981 and 1990, it was below 30 animals, and pneumonia was suspected to limit its growth, says Fisher. A survey in the fall of 1990 found only 14 sheep, but biologists estimated the actual number to be 30.Testing if the danger had passedIn January 1991, biologists set up an experiment. They released six radio-collared rams from Red Rock into the Peloncillos and monitored them until 30 June. The main objective was to see whether the resident lambs and the new rams contracted clinical pneumonia from the Arizona sheep already present in the flock. The researchers predicted that rams would die within four months if pneumonia was still active, based on the deaths of the early 1980s. They didn't. Except for one ram, all met the existing herd of 38 sheep, a count higher than the fall 1990 estimate of 30. No clinical signs of pneumonia were observed in any of the sheep, including lambs, and all the released rams were alive at the end. Fisher wrote that the herd was presently considered clinically free of pneumonia. She also said the herd was still not increasing because of low lamb survival in the southern Peloncillos, with the ratio of 35 lambs to 100 ewes. This suggested that there could be other problems.What later research addsMore recent studies have provided insight into why contact between sheep is so dangerous. According to the review, ‘Pneumonia in Bighorn Sheep: Risk and Resilience,’ by E. Frances Cassirer and team, in the Journal of Wildlife Management, reports of pneumonia outbreaks in wild bighorns due to contact with domestic sheep have been supported through captive tests. It says that a bacterium known as Mycoplasma ovipneumoniae, which is regularly found in healthy domestic sheep and goats, seems to be the main source of the disease. The review also notes that once a bacterium enters a bighorn population, it can remain there for decades. Fisher's report does not say that domestic sheep were involved in the 1981 deaths, so this research is background on how the disease works, not an explanation of what went down in the Peloncillos.A more recent study by Colton J. Padilla and colleagues published in Ecosphere in 2025 shows that from 2007 to 2022 the team had sampled 466 bighorn sheep from 19 New Mexico populations. The ratio of young sheep to adult females fell by 20% to 69% in the seven populations where it declined, and the drop was seen in both desert and Rocky Mountain populations after exposure to the bacterium. The authors suggested that these herds may be limited by lamb survival. The germ that caused the 1981 deaths isn't named in Fisher's report, so we can't tell if it was the same bacterium. Later studies showed that contact followed by illness is a known risk, and that it can have lingering effects in a herd.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran, Ukraine and an uneasy Europe: G7 weighs fallout of Trump's election blow
articles.summary: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in Paris on Monday with one major question hanging over the discussions.
articles.body: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in Paris on Monday with one major question hanging over the discussions. Will Donald Trump's midterm election setback change Washington's approach to the world's biggest geopolitical conflicts?As European allies assess the political fallout, the focus is on whether a weakened Trump will rethink his policies on Iran, Ukraine and relations with Europe.According to a Reuters report, citing four G7 diplomats, foreign ministers are seeking to assess whether the Republicans' midterm election setback will limit Trump's ability to pursue his foreign policy agenda.While Democratic gains could narrow the White House's room for manoeuvre, diplomats cautioned against expecting a return to traditional US multilateralism, as foreign policy decisions remain largely under Trump's control.Iran is expected to feature prominently at the Paris meeting, with European allies increasingly concerned that further US military action could deepen the conflict rather than bring it closer to an end. Washington's partners have repeatedly expressed scepticism over the war, which has also emerged as one of the issues behind Trump's electoral setback.US secretary of state Marco Rubio, speaking ahead of the meeting, played down the possibility of an imminent agreement with Tehran, saying negotiations were far from a breakthrough.He argued that Iran's demands were unacceptable and said leaders sometimes had to continue with unpopular policies if they believed they were necessary.Ukraine war raises fears of Europe being sidelinedUkraine is emerging as another major point of concern, with European allies worried that Washington could negotiate an end to the war with Moscow without giving European governments an adequate role.The G7 meeting comes ahead of trilateral discussions between Ukraine, Russia and the United States in Abu Dhabi, where efforts will focus on ending the conflict and discussing post-war security arrangements.The divisions are also exposing a lack of unity within Europe. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has warned that Europe risks becoming irrelevant in efforts to end the war if individual countries continue pursuing separate diplomatic initiatives instead of agreeing on a common representative and strategy.Meanwhile, diplomats have warned that Russia is increasingly targeting Ukraine's energy infrastructure to trigger widespread power shortages during winter. articles.title: A Kentucky father named as sole owner of the family home tried to evict his two adult sons after his wife died in 2025; a November 6 court refused to override protective orders keeping him 500 feet away
articles.summary: A Kentucky court has rejected a father's attempt to overturn protective orders that stop him from coming within 500 feet of his family home.
articles.body: A Kentucky court has rejected a father's attempt to overturn protective orders that stop him from coming within 500 feet of his family home. His two adult sons can continue living in the house, even though he claims to be its sole owner. The Kentucky Court of Appeals ruled on 6 November 2026 that the 500-foot restriction must remain in place. In its decision in Ashour Hamid v. Ahmad Hamid, et al. (Docket No. 2025-CA-1492-MR), the appeals court upheld the lower court's order protecting the sons and preventing their father from returning to the property. The ruling makes clear that owning a property does not automatically give someone the right to ignore valid court orders issued to protect family members from domestic violence or other harmful behavior under Kentucky law.Domestic disputes follow mother's deathThe legal dispute began after a serious family breakdown that grew worse following the death of Ashour Hamid's wife in 2025. Ashour Hamid is the sole legal owner of the family's home in Kentucky. After his wife died, he tried to regain full control of the property and remove his two adult sons, Ahmad Hamid and his brother, who had continued living there. However, existing court orders prevented him from doing so. Earlier legal proceedings had resulted in protective orders against Ashour Hamid following domestic disputes. These orders stopped him from approaching his sons or coming within 500 feet of the family home. Wanting to return to the property and remove his sons, Ashour Hamid filed legal requests asking the court to cancel or change the 500-foot restriction. He argued that because his name was the only one on the property's deed, his constitutional property rights gave him the right to live there and decide who could stay in the house.Trial court enforces strict boundary limitsThe trial court rejected Ashour Hamid's request to change the distance restriction. It decided that protecting the sons' safety was more important than the father's immediate right to take possession of the property. The court explained that domestic violence and interpersonal protective orders are designed to prevent physical harm, harassment and further family disputes. Since the existing order clearly stopped Ashour Hamid from coming within 500 feet of the people it protected, allowing him to return to the family home would make the order ineffective. After the trial court refused to remove the distance restriction, Ashour Hamid appealed to the Kentucky Court of Appeals. He asked the higher court to overturn the decision under docket number 2025-CA-1492-MR.Court of Appeals affirms protective boundariesIn an opinion issued on 6 November 2026, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's decision in full. This means the 500-foot restriction remains in place. The appeals court found that trial judges have broad authority to issue, manage and enforce protective orders. The judges explained that being the sole owner of a property does not give someone the right to remove safety restrictions that prevent contact with or protect other household members. Under Kentucky civil procedure rules and domestic violence laws, courts can restrict property owners from entering their own homes when such limits are considered necessary to prevent unwanted contact, intimidation or harm. The court also found that Ashour Hamid had failed to provide a valid legal reason to cancel or change the protective order. As a result, his two adult sons can continue living in the family home, while their father remains legally prohibited from coming within 500 feet of the property.You use AI every day. articles.title: ​In 2014, a Mona Vale beachfront house sold for A$7.65 million; twelve years later, it has been bought for A$29 million in a private sale, smashing the Sydney suburb’s previous record of A$13.5 million
articles.summary: A Mona Vale beachfront house, once owned by Australia’s McDonald’s boss, has sold for $29 million in an off-market deal.
articles.body: A Mona Vale beachfront house, once owned by Australia’s McDonald’s boss, has sold for $29 million in an off-market deal. The sale has set a new property record for the Northern Beaches suburb, more than doubling its previous benchmark of $13.5 million, set in October 2025. The sprawling beach house was bought by poker player Tom Rafferty and his wife, Milly.An off-market dealThe home at 27–29 Surfview Road was sold off-market. It never went to a public auction or an open listing. Joshua Perry of Bell Property Dee Why, who handled the deal, said the owners did not want strangers walking through the house. “It was really a one-on-one discreet buyer process. The owner didn’t want the home marketed to the masses. They simply wanted one particular buyer who was well-suited to the property – so that’s what we did. We approached the vendor with the purchaser,” Perry told the outlet. While homes of this calibre are typically marketed widely, this sale was handled privately.Setting a new recordUntil this month, the record for the most expensive home sale in Mona Vale was held by the mansion at 1 Bruce Street, which sold for $13.5 million in October 2025, Mona Vale News reported. It was a five-bedroom residence overlooking Warriewood Beach on a 657-square-metre block. Joshua Perry himself handled the sale and listing.This Surfview Road sale nearly doubles that figure in one deal. The land covers 2,056 square metres, and the house was designed by Peter Burford in a pavilion style, with level lawns running down to the sand. “It’s good to see that record jump from $13.5m up to nearly $30m,” Perry told the outlet. This jump is significant given that Sydney’s property market has depreciated in recent years.A single sale does not prove that prices across the suburb are climbing. However, it shows how much a rare beachfront property can fetch when the right buyer comes along.“I think once you get up to that echelon of people, they’re not holding back when everyone else is scared. When they find the property they want, they’re happy to pay for it and even pay what a lot of people would deem above market value if they feel it’s a rare offering,” he added.Previous ownersThe property belonged to Leigh and Peter Ritchie, the former chief executive of McDonald’s Australia. A listing record shows they sold it through a private treaty in December 2014 to former Goodman and BlackRock executive James Quille and his wife, Gillian, for $7.65 million. The Quilles lived in the mansion for more than a decade before handing over the keys. The couple are moving to Mosman, where they reportedly paid about $30 million for a Coronation Avenue mansion. That house, too, has a famous history. It was once used by Justin Bieber and Adele during their separate Australian tours.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Five euros is one kilo of tomatoes': Unions dismiss France's 24-euro minimum wage increase
articles.summary: French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday announced a modest increase in the minimum wage from December 1 in response to mounting cost-of-living
articles.body: French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday announced a modest increase in the minimum wage from December 1 in response to mounting cost-of-living protests, but trade unions swiftly dismissed the move as inadequate, saying it fell far short of workers' demands.Following meetings with representatives of employers' organisations and trade unions, Lecornu announced a 1.6% increase, which will raise the monthly minimum wage by around 24 euros to approximately 1,502 euros net. The increase comprises a 1% adjustment for inflation and an additional 0.6% boost.The announcement comes after weeks of demonstrations over wages, rising living costs and deteriorating public services. The protests, which began with high school blockades in September, have since expanded into a broader movement involving students, workers and other groups dissatisfied with the government's economic and political response.The proposed increase falls considerably short of demands from France's largest trade unions. The CFDT had called for a 100-euro monthly increase, while the hard-left CGT sought a rise of around 150 euros.CFDT general secretary Marylise Leon described the government's offer as "insufficient", while CGT leader Sophie Binet dismissed the additional five euros a month, beyond the automatic inflation adjustment, as "crumbs"."Five euros is one kilo of tomatoes," Binet said to Reuters, reiterating that a limited increase would do little to ease the financial pressures facing households.The minimum wage currently stands at around 1,478 euros net per month, following a 35-euro increase in June to account for inflation. Labour minister Jean-Pierre Farandou had previously said he wanted the figure to cross 1,500 euros, provided an increase did not damage employment.Farandou had also warned against a sharp rise, arguing that raising the minimum wage to 1,700 euros net could destroy more than 230,000 jobs.France adjusts its minimum wage for inflation every January, while the last discretionary increase dates back to 2012.Protests spread beyond schoolsThe government's announcement follows several weeks of demonstrations that have spread well beyond educational institutions. The protests began with high school blockades in September and have since drawn students, workers and other groups frustrated by rising living costs and the state of public services.Lecornu had sought to signal a change in approach ahead of Monday's meetings. In a letter to union leaders on Friday, he stressed the importance of social dialogue and engagement with unions and civil society.However, the government's ability to offer more substantial concessions remains constrained by France's deteriorating public finances. The country's public debt stands at around 3.6 trillion euros, or 120% of gross domestic product, while its budget deficit is 5.4%.Union representatives have questioned whether Lecornu can deliver meaningful relief to households under these financial constraints.The dispute also comes as France approaches its presidential election next year. President Emmanuel Macron, who is completing his second term and cannot seek re-election, faces low approval ratings, while opinion polls suggest far-right candidate Marine Le Pen could face hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon in a run-off.Le Pen has opposed a mandatory 10% increase in the minimum wage, arguing that businesses are too financially vulnerable to absorb it. Melenchon's La France Insoumise, meanwhile, has backed the protesters' demands. Its coordinator Manuel Bompard said on Sunday that addressing the crisis required an immediate political response to the financial pressures facing households.Candidates from the political centre have also struggled to position themselves amid the unrest. Edouard Philippe, the centre-right Horizons candidate, said minimum wage levels should be determined through negotiations between employers and unions rather than imposed by the government.The immediate challenge for Lecornu is whether Monday's announcement will ease public anger or further fuel calls for a more substantial increase. Public sector unions have already called for a strike and demonstrations on November 17, signalling that the mobilisation could continue in the coming weeks.You use AI every day. articles.body: French officials on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of carrying out cyberattacks that disrupted commercial refrigerators and freezers across France last month, warning that Tehran would face consequences.The attacks, which struck hundreds of supermarkets in early October, overrode temperature controls on commercial refrigeration units, causing food to rot and, in some cases, refrigerators to catch fire. French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the Iranian ambassador had been summoned to the foreign ministry and threatened further European Union sanctions against Iran.The announcement came shortly after a Reuters report revealed that French investigators privately suspected Iran of being behind the attacks. But Tehran has routinely denied conducting malicious cyber operations.The October 11 attack appeared relatively easy to execute, cybersecurity experts had earlier told Reuters. The manufacturer of several affected units said some were obsolete or running outdated firmware, potentially leaving them vulnerable to hackers.The attacks were followed this month by another wave of hacking that affected more than 100 establishments across Europe, including refrigeration units used by French blood banks. Staff were forced to move some blood supplies to alternative cold-storage facilities.The incidents have raised questions about the wider campaign and its possible links to other suspected cyber operations amid the ongoing US-Iran war, concerns over Russian sabotage in Europe and the growing use of artificial intelligence in cyberattacks.Similar incidents were reported in the United States before the French attacks. In August, refrigerators at at least half a dozen military commissaries stopped working. articles.title: A CEO's affair usually isn't national news. Here's why Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's is.
articles.summary: Who is Jensen Huang and why is Nvidia investigating his extramarital affair?
articles.body:
Nvidia's board of directors said Sunday it was launching an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang being the target of an alleged Chinese spy, with whom he had an affair.

Huang admitted to the affair in an email to Nvidia employees and is cooperating with the investigation. Reports have identified Alice Huang (no relation), former executive at tech firm Megaspeed, as the person he had the relationship with.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Jensen Huang said in a statement.

If you haven't been following the stock market closely, you may not be familiar with Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies. And you may be wondering why U.S. security officials would be concerned about a CEO's extramarital affair. Here's what we know so far, and why this tech CEO's affair is a big deal.

Jensen Huang is the CEO of Nvidia, one of the biggest makers of specialized computer chips in the world. Its chips were initially designed for computer graphics, but with the AI boom of the past few years, demand for Nvidia's hardware has skyrocketed. China and the U.S. are in a heated competition for AI technology, and that includes access to chips like the ones Nvidia makes.

Jensen Huang is an American citizen who was born in Taiwan. He founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been the company's president and CEO since, steering the company through the AI boom of the past several years.

According to the New York Times, it's unclear when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang — an alleged Chinese spy — but the two were photographed together in 2024 at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan. It was roughly around that time when Megaspeed, the AI company she worked for, began its push into the AI sector. Multiple news reports were unable to confirm if Alice Huang is still employed at Megaspeed today. Megaspeed has touted its membership in Nvidia's partnership program, which would provide access to its latest technology.

Huang apologized for the affair in a message to Nvidia employees, and asked for privacy for his family. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused," Huang wrote, "and I accept the criticism that comes with it."

He pledged to earn back his employees' confidence, and added that he was cooperating fully with the board's investigation. "I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security," he wrote.

The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was gathering information for the Chinese government. China denied that it was spying , calling the allegation unsubstantiated. "It is nothing but smears against China," a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said.

The New York Times also reported that executives at Nvidia contacted the U.S. Commerce Department last year seeking information about the department's investigation into Megaspeed. The investigation was later transferred to the Department of Justice, which is reportedly looking into Megaspeed's involvement in potentially illegally routing Nvidia products into China.

AI is the biggest thing in tech right now, infiltrating our lives via chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, and disrupting all sorts of industries from software development and bioengineering. Governments are trying to determine how and when to use AI for security and across business sectors too. China and the U.S. are hastily competing to dominate AI development for uses across multiple industries. The development has been so rapid that some CEOs of AI companies have suggested a pause may be in order before the technology develops beyond what humans can control.

Nvidia has contracts with the U.S. government to use its technology in several areas , and Jensen Huang has a close relationship with President Trump. U.S. officials are trying to determine if the affair may have allowed the Chinese government to receive information about Nvidia's technology and its agreements with the U.S. government. Nvidia's board said in its statement that the company does not believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.

President Trump said late Sunday that he considers Huang "a fine person" who should stay on as CEO of Nvidia.

"I think he probably has an excuse for it. We'll have to hear it," Trump told reporters Sunday night. "He's done an amazing job for our country."

articles.title: Megan Thee Stallion's foundation joined Habitat for Humanity to repair more than 30 homes in Texas; the project will help older residents remain independent
articles.summary: A housing initiative launched earlier this year in Houston and Dallas brought together Megan Thee Stallion’s charitable foundation and one of the United
articles.body: A housing initiative launched earlier this year in Houston and Dallas brought together Megan Thee Stallion’s charitable foundation and one of the United States' largest housing organisations. The collaboration is focused on older homeowners whose properties need repairs or accessibility improvements to remain suitable for everyday living. Through her Pete & Thomas Foundation, the Grammy-winning artist partnered with Habitat for Humanity to support work on more than 30 homes across the two Texas cities. The planned improvements range from roofing and structural repairs to ramps and other mobility features, addressing some of the difficulties older residents face when trying to remain in homes they have occupied for years.How Megan Thee Stallion’s foundation plans to improve homes for older TexansThe partnership was announced on April 30, 2026, with the first phase beginning on May 2 in Houston’s South Park neighbourhood. The initiative brought the Pete & Thomas Foundation into Habitat for Humanity’s existing Aging in Place programme, which provides repairs and home modifications for older homeowners.More than 30 properties in Houston and Dallas were included in the project. The planned work covers several areas of home maintenance, including roofing, weatherproofing, structural stabilisation and ramp installations. Other modifications are intended to make properties easier to navigate for residents experiencing mobility difficulties.For older homeowners, these improvements can affect how comfortably they manage everyday activities. A damaged roof, deteriorating structure or entrance that is difficult to access can create problems that become harder to deal with over time. Repairing these features can help residents continue living in familiar surroundings rather than having to consider moving because their homes no longer meet their needs.Why nearly 77% of older Americans want to remain in their homesThe project addresses a housing concern affecting a growing number of older Americans. Many prefer to remain in their own homes as they age, keeping their established routines and connections with their neighbourhoods. However, the condition and design of some properties can make independent living more difficult.Figures from AARP cited by Habitat for Humanity indicate that nearly 77% of older adults want to remain in their homes over the long term. Yet many houses were not originally designed to accommodate changing mobility needs. Others have maintenance problems that residents may find difficult to manage or afford.Habitat's Aging in Place programme works with local organisations and community groups to assess individual homeowners' requirements. Depending on the property, assistance can include essential repairs, accessibility modifications and other services intended to help residents maintain their independence.Megan Thee Stallion Day marked the Houston project launch in MayThe first repair activities began on May 2 in South Park, Houston. The date coincided with Megan Thee Stallion Day, an annual city recognition established in 2022 to honour the artist and her contributions to the community.Volunteers from Hotties Helping, a community initiative associated with the Pete & Thomas Foundation, joined Habitat volunteers during the launch. Their activities included painting, caulking and landscaping around participating properties.The launch also coincided with the beginning of Older Americans Month in May, which recognises the contributions of older people and highlights the support they need to maintain their health, independence and quality of life.Habitat for Humanity marked the occasion by temporarily renaming its Let's Open the Door campaign to Let's Open Thee Door. Launched in March 2026, the campaign was created to raise awareness of housing challenges and encourage action. The temporary name referenced Megan's stage identity while drawing attention to the need for safer and more accessible homes for older residents.What Megan said about supporting older generationsMegan Thee Stallion said that looking after older adults had long been an important part of her charitable work. In her statement announcing the collaboration, she explained that maintaining safe and properly cared-for homes was part of supporting the generations that came before her.She also described the partnership as an effort that extended beyond physical repairs, with the intention of giving older homeowners greater peace of mind about their living conditions.The Pete & Thomas Foundation was established in February 2022 in memory of Megan's late parents, Holly Thomas and Joseph Pete III. The organisation was created to support women, children, senior citizens and underserved communities.Its activities are organised around four main areas: education, housing, health and wellness, and community goodwill. The Habitat for Humanity partnership falls under its housing work, with a focus on helping older residents access the repairs and infrastructure needed to remain in their homes.Habitat for Humanity highlights the connection between housing and healthHabitat for Humanity has linked the condition of a person's home with their ability to maintain good health and independence. For older residents, problems such as unstable structures, poor weather protection and difficult entrances can affect their daily routines and make independent living more challenging.Adrienne Goolsby, senior vice president of US and Canada at Habitat for Humanity International, said the collaboration was intended to advance housing and health equity for older adults. The organisation's Aging in Place programme aims to help residents remain in their communities through repairs and modifications suited to their circumstances.Allison Hay, chief executive of Houston Habitat for Humanity, also highlighted the importance of improving homes in neighbourhoods such as South Park. As a Houston resident herself, she pointed to the need for older homeowners to have properties that can better withstand future Gulf Coast weather events.The planned improvements therefore address both everyday housing conditions and the challenges posed by severe weather. Roofing work, structural repairs and weatherproofing can help address existing maintenance issues, while accessibility changes are intended to make homes easier to use as residents grow older.The Pete & Thomas Foundation expands its housing workThe collaboration with Habitat for Humanity adds a practical dimension to the Pete & Thomas Foundation's housing efforts. Rather than focusing on building new properties, this initiative is centred on improving existing homes and helping the people who live in them.The more than 30 homes identified across Houston and Dallas were included in a programme of repairs based on individual property requirements. Some may need roofing or weatherproofing work, while others require structural improvements, ramps or mobility-related modifications.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Utah family owned its farm for at least 70 years beside a fence in place since 1965; a neighbour's 2021 survey challenged the boundary, but a November 5 appeals ruling let the family keep the disputed strip of land
articles.summary: Decades of farming and a boundary fence that has stood since 1965 have helped a Utah family keep its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland.
articles.body: Decades of farming and a boundary fence that has stood since 1965 have helped a Utah family keep its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland. A state appeals court has ruled in the family's favour after a neighbouring landowner challenged the property boundary. The Utah Court of Appeals issued its decision on 5 November 2026, upholding a trial court ruling in favour of the Christiansen Family Trust. The court rejected a challenge brought by a company that owns the neighbouring property. The decision in Christiansen Family Trust v. Haas Land & Livestock (Case No. 20251107-CA) settles a long-running property dispute in Utah. It confirms that when neighbouring landowners accept and use a physical fence as their boundary for many years, that boundary can take legal priority over a newer land survey. Writing for the unanimous appeals panel, Judge Ryan M. Harris found that the trial court correctly applied Utah's legal rule known as boundary by acquiescence. This rule protects property boundaries that neighbours have accepted over a long period. Judges John D. Luthy and Amy J. Oliver agreed with the decision.Boundary survey triggers conflict over farm landThe Christiansen family has owned and actively farmed its rural Utah property for more than 70 years. Farming activities have continued across several generations. For nearly six decades, a fence built in 1965 marked the boundary between the Christiansen family's farm and the neighbouring property. Both the Christiansen family and previous owners of the adjoining land treated the fence as the actual property line. Each side continued farming, grazing animals and maintaining its own land without any disagreement over the boundary. The peaceful arrangement changed after Haas Land & Livestock bought the neighbouring property in 2021. After purchasing the land, Haas Land & Livestock hired a professional surveyor to identify its exact property boundaries. The survey found that the legal boundary listed in the property deed did not match the location of the old fence built in 1965. According to the survey markers, a narrow strip of land that the Christiansen family had occupied and farmed was actually included in the legal description of the neighbouring property. Based on these findings, Haas Land & Livestock claimed ownership of the disputed strip and tried to take control of it. This led to a legal battle over who had the rightful ownership of the land.Trial court applies doctrine of boundary by acquiescenceThe Christiansen Family Trust filed a lawsuit in state district court. It argued that it had legal ownership of the disputed land under Utah's long-standing rule known as boundary by acquiescence.Under Utah property law, a landowner may gain permanent legal ownership of land beyond the boundaries written in their deed if four specific conditions are met:There must be a visible marker, such as a fence, wall or monument, showing where the boundary is located.The person claiming the land must use and occupy their property up to that visible boundary in a way that clearly shows they are using the land.The neighbouring landowners must both treat and accept the visible marker as the actual property boundary.Both sides must continue accepting and following that boundary without interruption for at least 20 years.During the trial, the Christiansen family presented evidence showing that the fence had remained in place since 1965. They also showed that both sides had treated it as the dividing line for much longer than the required 20-year period. Haas Land & Livestock challenged the trust's ownership claim and tried to present video evidence during the court proceedings. However, the trial judge refused to admit the footage and ruled in favour of the Christiansen Family Trust. The judge found that clear and convincing evidence proved all the legal requirements for boundary by acquiescence had been met. Haas Land & Livestock then appealed to the Utah Court of Appeals. The company argued that the trial court's findings were not supported by enough evidence. It also claimed that refusing to accept the video footage was a serious legal error that justified overturning the decision.Appellate court affirms historical boundary lineThe Utah Court of Appeals rejected all the company's arguments. It found that the trial court had acted correctly in awarding the disputed strip of land to the Christiansen family. Judge Ryan M. Harris wrote that the trial court's findings were supported by the evidence presented during the case. The appeals panel confirmed that the fence had existed since 1965 and that previous owners on both sides had accepted it as the property boundary for many years. This was enough to establish legal ownership under Utah law. "The court ruled that the trial court's findings were supported by sufficient evidence and that the exclusion of the video evidence was not an abuse of discretion," the appellate panel noted in its ruling, as reported by legal news service LAWS.com. The court also explained that Utah law does not require neighbours to sign a written agreement to establish a boundary through long-term acceptance. Instead, years of accepting, recognising and following a physical fence line can be enough to establish legal ownership over time. The judges also found that the trial court had the legal authority to reject the video footage submitted by the defendant. Decisions about which evidence can be used during a trial are generally left to the trial judge's judgment, and the court found no reason to overturn that decision.Broader implications for Utah property ownersThe appeals court's decision offers important guidance to property owners, farmers and real estate developers across Utah. It explains how courts may handle disputes involving old fence lines and newer land surveys. Legal analysts at legal publisher LAWS.com noted that the ruling highlights how courts give significant weight to the way land has actually been used over many years, especially when a long-established boundary is challenged by a newer technical survey. By ruling that 56 years of continuous and undisputed use of the fence line took priority over a survey conducted in 2021, the Utah Court of Appeals reinforced an important point for property buyers. People who purchase older rural properties may have to respect existing, visible boundaries that have been accepted and used by neighbouring landowners over a long period. The ruling leaves the Christiansen Family Trust with full legal ownership and control of the disputed strip, protecting the family's farm boundaries as they have stood since 1965.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ghaziabad blast probe finds no evidence of IED at Vasundhara police outpost
articles.summary: Ghaziabad blast probe at Vasundhara police outpost finds no IED evidence; agencies probe AC fault or stray firecracker as ATS, NIA, STF join.
articles.body: Ghaziabad: Preliminary searches at Vasundhara police outpost, which was rocked by an explosion on Friday night, have found no explosive residue, gunpowder, chemical traces or identifiable components of an improvised explosive device (IED). No detonator, battery, connecting wires or other material suggesting a bomb has been recovered, leaving agencies without physical evidence so far to support a deliberate attack.Police are examining other causes, including an electrical fault in an air-conditioner and seized illegal firecrackers stored at the outpost. They are also checking if a firecracker struck the AC unit. Forensic samples have been sent to Agra for analysis.“The cause of the explosion has not been established yet. We are investigating every angle. Further action will be based on findings,” Ghaziabad police commissioner J Ravinder Goud said.DCP (trans-Hindon) Rijul Kumar also said initial checks found no explosives, gunpowder or chemical residue. The blast, around 9pm on Nov 6, shattered two windowpanes and cracked a wall. A delivery worker suffered cuts from flying glass, while a sub-inspector on duty escaped unhurt.Officials said they were also assessing if the outpost’s condition magnified the damage. The 21-year-old building had deteriorated and was allegedly built with substandard material.Police are checking whether an object was thrown from Hindon Elevated Road, around 35ft above the outpost. Municipal corporation cameras along Shri Ram Setu elevated road were allegedly not working, so teams are relying on traffic police footage and plan to analyse mobile tower records.The terror angle emerged after an X account, ‘Ghazi 2’, posted a video and statement around 2.30am on Nov 7, claiming responsibility for Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen Hindustan. The account has since been deleted. Police are seeking information from X to identify its operators and verify the group’s role. The masked speaker in the video called the blast an attack on police.UP ATS, led by DIG Abhishek Yadav, is leading the probe, while NIA, STF, IB and Delhi Police’s special cell are also involved. articles.summary: Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, pitched a multimillion-dollar artificial intelligence infrastructure project to
articles.body: Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, pitched a multimillion-dollar artificial intelligence infrastructure project to investors, claiming she could secure the US company's advanced chips and citing Chinese technology giant Alibaba as a prospective client, according to a Financial Times report.Alice Huang and her business partner Kang Wei sought investment in early 2025 for a Southeast Asian data-centre project estimated to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars, the FT reported, citing two investors who were approached about the proposal.During the pitch, the pair said they had no problem securing Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), a key component used to develop and operate artificial intelligence systems. They also cited Alibaba as a client for the proposed project, according to an investor familiar with the discussions.The development adds another dimension to the scrutiny surrounding Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, following allegations that she was recruited by Chinese intelligence to establish a relationship with Jensen Huang and potentially influence his position on US restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.The allegations have not been independently established. Beijing has rejected the espionage claims, while Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing related to chip smuggling.Questions over Nvidia chips and China linksThe proposed data-centre project also raises questions about how advanced Nvidia chips could be made available to Chinese businesses through infrastructure located outside mainland China.US export controls restrict Chinese companies from owning certain advanced AI chips, although Chinese businesses can lease computing capacity from data centres operating overseas, subject to applicable restrictions.The FT report said Alice Huang and Kang Wei presented access to Nvidia GPUs as a central part of their investment proposal. Their reference to Alibaba also drew attention to the Chinese technology company's reported business relationship with Megaspeed.Documents reviewed by the FT investigation showed that Alibaba had lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries in 2024. People familiar with the company described Alibaba as Megaspeed's anchor customer and largest client.Jensen Huang faces growing scrutinyThe latest revelations come as Nvidia faces questions over its chief executive's reported relationship with Alice Huang and whether the company was exposed to a potential foreign intelligence operation.US intelligence officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was connected to a Chinese espionage effort targeting Jensen Huang. The alleged objective was to gather information about the Nvidia chief and influence his efforts to persuade Washington to ease restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China.Jensen Huang has acknowledged having an extramarital affair and apologized to his wife and family. Nvidia's independent directors have launched an investigation into whether he was targeted in a foreign intelligence operation.The company has said it has no reason to believe that its national security interests or confidential information were compromised. The allegations have nevertheless brought renewed attention to Nvidia's business dealings in China and the security implications of its global AI chip supply chain.You use AI every day. articles.title: AI fire video sends 20 fire teams rushing to a blaze that never happened
articles.summary: AI-generated fire video on X falsely claimed a blaze at Noida Sector 119 high-rise, prompting 20 fire teams to respond; police filed cybercrime FIR.
articles.body: Noida: An AI-generated video of a massive fire at a residential high-rise in Sector 119 sent police and fire officials into a frenzy, with 20 fire teams from four districts rushing to the spot before authorities found that no such incident had occurred.The video, widely circulated on X, purportedly showed flames engulfing a flat on the 21st floor of The Aranya. Police have registered an FIR at the cybercrime police station and are tracing the accounts that uploaded and amplified the footage.A senior police officer said the department took up the case after the video surfaced online. Given that the blaze was reported on an upper floor of a residential tower, emergency teams were dispatched immediately.Firefighters found no flames, smoke or damage. A subsequent examination of the footage showed that it had been created using artificial intelligence to portray a fabricated emergency.Police said the clip was uploaded and circulated through multiple accounts on X. One of the profiles identified in connection with its circulation operated under the name “Sachin Kashyap Journalist”.Investigators are trying to identify the original creator of the video and establish whether it was circulated deliberately to create panic. They will examine the digital trail associated with the posts to determine who generated the content and how it spread across social media platforms.
